server_info.name: SVC Agent API
server_info.description: Read authorized SVC data and safely use the write operations authorized for this connection.

owner/all_scopes.instructions: First call context.get; select only workspace and resource IDs returned by SVC and never guess an ID. For time tracking, use projects.list to match projects, tasks.list only when available and needed, and time_entries.log for completed work with the exact date, whole minutes, description, and a stable idempotency key. Reuse a key only for an identical retry and never approve time unless the user asks. Read an existing record before updating or deleting it and supply its current opaque version. Authorized write tools are enabled for this connection. Read the current record before mutation and supply its opaque version when required. When the user asks to approve time they are logging, pass approve: true to time_entries.log instead of a separate approve call; with time:read and while time_entries.list remains enabled, it returns the rows as time_entries.list does, otherwise it returns the plain write shape. Obtain explicit user confirmation before issue, send, void, correct, activating an agreement, terminating an agreement, expense_schedules.generate, releasing automatic delivery, or generating a cadence draft. Obtain explicit user confirmation before billing_schedules.generate: it issues invoices and may schedule automatic client delivery. Obtain explicit user confirmation before creating, updating, archiving projects or changing project member access; these decisions affect client visibility and access. Obtain explicit user confirmation before sending or accepting a proposal. Sending publishes it in the client portal without emailing. Acceptance signs and activates an agreement; require an explicit signer name and never infer acceptance from a request to read or create a proposal. Obtain explicit user confirmation before deleting an attachment. When the user confirms issuing a draft for money already collected elsewhere, pass payment to invoices.issue so it is issued and paid in one step and the automatic client delivery is never sent; never infer a payment from an invoice balance. Authenticate using OAuth Authorization Code with S256 PKCE. Invoice responses provide a browser URL for any payment flow; payments.record records money already received but never initiates a charge, and SVC does not expose card data or file uploads through MCP. Use the log-time-across-projects and prepare-invoice-safely prompts for complete guided workflows when the client exposes MCP prompts.

tools.name: billing.preflight_schedule_generation
tools.title: Preflight schedule generation
tools.description: Workspace managers only. Classify every period each of the workspace's active billing schedules is due to bill through today, without writing, and count how many schedules would halt and why, as svc:billing:preflight-schedule-generation does for every workspace. Counts only, including agreement_handover_overlap schedule defects. It examines at most 60 periods per schedule (the command examines 240), and complete is false when a backlog was longer, so the result is inconclusive rather than clean. A workspace gets 5 per ten minutes, then 429 with Retry-After.

tools.name: billing_audit.stale_and_missing
tools.title: Audit stale drafts and missing periods
tools.description: Workspace managers only. Count drafts whose due date or scheduled issue date has passed and active recurring agreements lacking a non-void invoice for their current retainer period, with balances per currency and up to 100 identifiers per category. Where Square serves the workspace, also flags invoices paid outside Square, billed Square series periods with no linked svc invoice, unrecorded Square payments, unlinked Square customers with an open balance, and series drift from the agreement. Also reports issued invoice coverage overlapping a successor agreement for review, without inferring whether it was prorated. Flags only: nothing is issued, sent or generated, and nothing is written to Square.

complete.description: False unless the newest sync run completed and listed every Square invoice (a run still going, failed or truncated leaves the mirror between generations), when the audit reached a bound (5,000 members of billed-in-Square series, 5,000 other mirrored invoices, 500 agreements, or 10,000 payment ids checked), or when the mirror has yet to read the payment ids of a paid invoice in reach. Every count is then a floor; series_not_mirrored needs a complete sync, series_drift is withheld when series members were bounded, and unlinked_customer_balances when other invoices were.

unmirrored_series_periods.description: Billed members of a series an agreement is billed in, within the agreement (from its start to its end, once it has one), with no svc invoice linked. SCHEDULED, DRAFT, CANCELED and FAILED members are not flagged.

unmatched_payments.description: Square payments on invoices in svc's reach - linked, in a billed-in-Square series, or of a confirmed customer - that svc has not recorded under provider square.

unlinked_customer_balances.description: Square customers with no client company mapped and an open invoice, most owed first: the customers square.customers.unlinked lists with an open balance.

series_drift.description: Billed-in-Square agreements whose billed members since the agreement began (SCHEDULED ones are not yet billed) differ in cadence, currency (another, or more than one) or latest amount, whose series the mirror does not hold, or whose series prefix is used in more than one Square location.

SquareBillingAudit.description: Phase-two Square billing-audit flags, read from svc's mirror as of its last sync. Empty where Square does not serve the workspace. Nothing here writes to Square.

square_location_id.description: The Square location the agreement's series bills from; null for a marker set before markers named a location, which takes the prefix in every location.

codes.description: multiple_locations: the series prefix is used in more than one Square location among the bills since the agreement began, which Square allows; the series is not compared, and no unmirrored period or unmatched payment is derived from it. billed_after_end: Square billed a member after the agreement ended.

agreement_cadence.description: Null when the agreement does not bill on a repeating cycle.

series_cadence.description: Read from the spacing of the billed members' due dates; unknown with fewer than two dated billed members, and null when the mirror holds no member.

series_currency.description: The billed members' one currency; null when they were billed in more than one, which is currency drift.

agreement_amount.description: The retainer fee for one whole cycle, in minor units; null when the agreement sells none, and it is then not compared.

series_amount.description: The latest billed member's amount, in minor units.

SquareSeriesKey.description: A Square recurring series: the six-digit prefix of its invoices' NNNNNN-R-NNNN numbers.

currency.description: Null when the open invoices are in more than one currency.

open_amount.description: Minor units; null when the open invoices are in more than one currency or one of them has no known amount.

reason.description: not_recorded: the Square invoice is linked, but svc holds no Square payment with this id. invoice_not_linked: the Square invoice is in a billed-in-Square series or belongs to a confirmed customer, and no svc invoice is linked to it.

through.description: The day the backlog is read as of: the workspace's today, or the day before a successor agreement for the same project scope takes over. Later work is not on it.

hours.description: Every hour the termination invoice would bill today: the outstanding deferred entries plus carried_hours. Null only when withheld.

agreement_rate_hours.description: Consultant and retainer-mode hours, priced at the agreement's hourly rate. Null when withheld or unpriced.

flat_hourly_hours.description: Flat-hourly subcontractor hours, priced at each entry's snapshotted rate. Null when withheld or unpriced.

carried_hours.description: Deferred hours an earlier invoice applied beyond free capacity, which the ledger carries forward as a quantity and termination bills on its own line at the agreement's rate. Included in hours and the amount. Null where the ledger was not read: always in operations.summary, and when the ledger refuses to build.

amount_at_hourly_rate.description: What the termination invoice would charge for these hours, in minor units of the agreement currency. Direct subcontractor work is never included.

issue_detail.description: The refusal behind issue: the pricing refusal termination would raise when unpriced, or the ledger refusal when ledger_unreadable.

net_hours_per_month.description: Average of added minus applied minus billed over the trend months; positive means the shelf is growing. Null without a trend.

DeferredBacklogIssue.description: project_chain_mismatch: a deferred entry points to a project outside the client, so termination would refuse and every figure is withheld. unpriced: the hours stand but termination would refuse to price them; the amount is null and issue_detail says why. ledger_unreadable: the agreement's capacity ledger refuses to build, so any re-carried balance termination would also bill is unknown; the figures exclude it and issue_detail says why.

period.description: Calendar month, as the capacity ledger names it.

hours_added.description: Deferred work done this month, whatever has happened to it since.

hours_applied.description: Deferred work a retainer pool of this month absorbed, booked on the ledger's capacity date.

hours_billed.description: Deferred work that left the shelf this month at an hourly price instead: on termination, as flat-hourly work, or by a buy-down.

hours_bought_down.description: Buy-down subset of hours_billed, excluded from retainer usage and not deducted twice from net shelf growth.

tools.name: finance.invoice_payments.list
tools.title: List payments for finance reconciliation
tools.description: Received payments with what each is worth net of refunds, how much of that its active finance reconciliation allocations cover, and every allocation, active first; newest received first. Succeeded payments unless status is given; status=any returns every status the enum names, so a full refund (refunded) and a partial one (still succeeded) are both seen; a row with an unrecognised status is never returned. 50 a page unless per_page is (at most 100), numbered by page. For incremental sync, name updated_since, watermark or cursor instead of page, with status=any (any other status, received_from and received_to are refused there: a payment can change out of them): payments then come newest change first (updated_at, then id) inside a snapshot watermark that the first page of a pass fixes (now, or an earlier time given) and every page returns in meta; follow meta.next_cursor until it is null, then start the next pass with updated_since set to that watermark (inclusive; starting a few seconds earlier is harmless). Timestamps only find candidates, and consecutive passes overlap: deduplicate by (id, version), where version also moves when one of the payment's allocations changes. The embedded invoice and client are read-time snapshots, not change-tracked: a change to the invoice or client does not move the payment, so follow invoices.list and clients.list for them. Payments are never deleted. A processor payment also carries what the processor reports about settling it: its own payment identifier, its charge time (not received_on, which for Stripe is the day svc heard of it), its fee, and the payout it settled in with that payout's arrival date; finance.payouts.list lists the payouts. These move the payment's version when the processor reports them. Workspace owners/admins; with the finance token, any workspace member. Internal ids and payment notes are never returned. The Sanctum finance token issued by svc:auth:issue-token is accepted too, its finance.read and finance.reconcile abilities standing for these scopes.

tools.name: finance.payouts.list
tools.title: List processor payouts for finance reconciliation
tools.description: The payment-processor payouts (Stripe, Square) that settled this workspace's payments: each payout's signed amount in minor units (negative when the payout took money from the bank account), currency, arrival date, type (automatic, manual or instant) and status (pending, in_transit, paid, failed or canceled); newest arrival first. Its member payments are the payments whose provider_payout_identifier names it, in finance.invoice_payments.list. Matching is net-only: a payout's amount is what reached the bank, and refunds, disputes or fees that land in a different payout, and manual or instant Stripe payouts (whose members Stripe does not list), are left for the finance system to treat as unexplained. A payout reported failed or canceled after it was reported paid stays so. 50 a page unless per_page is (at most 100), numbered by page. For incremental sync, name updated_since, watermark or cursor instead of page: the change feed works as on finance.invoice_payments.list (newest change first inside a snapshot watermark; deduplicate by (id, version)) and takes only the provider filter, since a payout's status and arrival date can change (status, arrival_from and arrival_to are refused there). Payouts are never deleted. Workspace owners/admins; with the finance token, any workspace member. The Sanctum finance token issued by svc:auth:issue-token is accepted too, its finance.read and finance.reconcile abilities standing for these scopes.

tools.name: finance.reconciliations.acknowledge

tools.description: Explicitly affirm that the allocation remains correct after its processor refund or dispute review. Requires confirm: true, the current payment version from finance.invoice_payments.list, and the exact review reason and timestamp shown on the allocation. Clears only that current review; allocated money and active state are retained even above payment net or on a disputed/refunded payment. Does not resolve a dispute, restore a payment, issue credit or move money. The payment version advances so synchronizers see the cleared flag. Conditional and idempotent by effect: no Idempotency-Key or replay receipt; repeating the original request, any stale payment version, a changed review, or an already-cleared flag returns 409 and requires a fresh read. Owner/admin only. The Sanctum finance token issued by svc:auth:issue-token is accepted too, its finance.read and finance.reconcile abilities standing for these scopes.

admin/all_scopes.instructions: First call context.get; select only workspace and resource IDs returned by SVC and never guess an ID. For time tracking, use projects.list to match projects, tasks.list only when available and needed, and time_entries.log for completed work with the exact date, whole minutes, description, and a stable idempotency key. Reuse a key only for an identical retry and never approve time unless the user asks. Read an existing record before updating or deleting it and supply its current opaque version. Authorized write tools are enabled for this connection. Read the current record before mutation and supply its opaque version when required. When the user asks to approve time they are logging, pass approve: true to time_entries.log instead of a separate approve call; with time:read and while time_entries.list remains enabled, it returns the rows as time_entries.list does, otherwise it returns the plain write shape. Obtain explicit user confirmation before issue, send, void, correct, activating an agreement, terminating an agreement, expense_schedules.generate, releasing automatic delivery, or generating a cadence draft. Obtain explicit user confirmation before billing_schedules.generate: it issues invoices and may schedule automatic client delivery. Obtain explicit user confirmation before creating, updating, archiving projects or changing project member access; these decisions affect client visibility and access. Obtain explicit user confirmation before sending or accepting a proposal. Sending publishes it in the client portal without emailing. Acceptance signs and activates an agreement; require an explicit signer name and never infer acceptance from a request to read or create a proposal. Obtain explicit user confirmation before deleting an attachment. When the user confirms issuing a draft for money already collected elsewhere, pass payment to invoices.issue so it is issued and paid in one step and the automatic client delivery is never sent; never infer a payment from an invoice balance. Authenticate using OAuth Authorization Code with S256 PKCE. Invoice responses provide a browser URL for any payment flow; payments.record records money already received but never initiates a charge, and SVC does not expose card data or file uploads through MCP. Use the log-time-across-projects and prepare-invoice-safely prompts for complete guided workflows when the client exposes MCP prompts.
